title: The No-Nonsense Guide to Corporate Cards for Small Businesses in 2026
summary: Compare the best corporate cards for UAE small businesses. Explore top expense management platforms and bank cards to find your perfect fit in 2026.
body_markdown:
Choosing a corporate card isn't just about earning cashback or travel rewards anymore. The right card influences how employees spend, how finance teams stay in control, and how easily businesses scale.


The timing couldn't be better. The[Central Bank of the UAE processed a record number of digital payments in 2024, while Dubai continues its push towards a 90% cashless economy by 2026.](https://www.khaleejtimes.com/business/uae-card-transactions-set-to-surge-to-dh5655-billion) As business spending shifts to cards, having the right expense management platform matters more than ever.


This guide compares the best corporate cards for businesses in the UAE and the leading global options.


## What to actually look for before you apply


Rewards points are the easy part to get distracted by. The things that save you real time every month are less exciting and more useful:


- Spend controls you can set per employee or per card, not just a single company-wide limit
- How many cards you can issue, and how fast - some banks cap you at a handful of supplementary cards; platforms like Alaan let you issue unlimited virtual and physical cards at no extra cost, which matters the moment you're hiring or scaling teams
- Real-time visibility into what's being spent, rather than a statement that lands three weeks later
- Receipt capture that doesn't rely on someone remembering to forward an email
- Accounting sync with whatever you already use, so a transaction doesn't need to be typed in twice
- Approval limits and eligibility that actually fit a small business, not a criteria list written for a 200-person company


Keep that list next to you. It's a better filter than any features page.


## Best corporate cards for small businesses in the UAE


### [1. Alaan SuperCard](https://www.alaan.com/supercard)


Built for UAE finance teams tired of managing spend after the fact.


- Card issuance: Unlimited virtual and physical Visa cards, instant, no extra cost
- Spend limits: Yes, by merchant, category, or amount
- Real-time visibility: Yes
- Receipt capture: Yes, auto-matched with automated VAT extraction
- Accounting sync: Xero, QuickBooks, and other major tools/ERPs
- Rewards: Up to 2% uncapped cashback on international spend (Premium/Enterprise), paid as cash, not points
- Eligibility: UAE-registered businesses, no personal guarantee
- Extras: ISO 27001 certified; liability waiver insurance up to $25K/employee


### [2. Emirates NBD Business Credit Card](https://www.emiratesnbd.com/en/cards/commercial-cards/business-credit-card)


The traditional route, and still a solid one if you already bank there.


- Card issuance: Supplementary cards allowed, but draw from one shared limit, not unlimited
- Spend limits: Set as a % of the primary limit, not fully independent per card
- Real-time visibility: Partial, via Visa Spend Clarity for Business
- Receipt capture: None
- Accounting sync: Yes, via Visa Spend Clarity for Business
- Rewards: Plus Points, capped at 500/statement; heavy spenders stop earning above that
- Eligibility: Trade licence, KYC, credit checks; branch-based approval


### [3. First Abu Dhabi Bank (FAB)](https://www.bankfab.com/en-ae/business-banking)


A three-tier SME Commercial Cards Suite with Mastercard.


- Card issuance: ONYX (World Elite), SILVER (commercial credit), and a World Debit Card linked to your FAB account, plus a mobile virtual card number (VCN) tool
- Spend limits: Yes, real-time controls across the suite
- Real-time visibility: Yes, via FAB's Business Application
- Receipt capture: Not a stated feature
- Accounting sync: Not specified beyond digital banking integration
- Rewards: Global merchant discount program
- Eligibility: FAB business banking relationship; documentation-based approval


### [4. Wio Business](https://wio.io/business)


Fully digital, backed by FAB, built for fast onboarding.


- Card issuance: Unlimited virtual cards, plus numberless physical cards
- Spend limits: Yes, set per card with full monitoring
- Real-time visibility: Yes
- Receipt capture: Not a stated feature
- Accounting sync: Not specified for the business tier
- Rewards: Cashback varies by plan; confirm current business-tier terms
- Eligibility: Digital onboarding, accessible to smaller businesses larger banks turn away


### [5. ADCB Business](https://www.adcb.com/en/business/products-solutions/corporate-cards/#all)


Known for single-use virtual cards for vendor payments.


- Card issuance: Multiple products (Corporate, Purchasing, TouchPoints, single-use virtual), but bank-controlled, not self-service
- Spend limits: Yes, via built-in budgeting tools
- Real-time visibility: Available through business banking tools
- Receipt capture: Not a stated feature
- Accounting sync: Positioned as "budgeting and expense management," not direct software sync
- Rewards: TouchPoints loyalty program on international/domestic spend
- Extras: Lounge access and travel insurance on select cards
- Eligibility: Standard bank documentation and approval timeline


**Best corporate cards for small businesses outside the UAE**


If you're setting up outside the UAE, or running a business with a presence in both places, the criteria shift slightly. US and global fintechs underwrite differently, and eligibility often depends more on funding status and cash balance than on a trade license.


### [1. Ramp](https://ramp.com/corporate-cards)


Default pick for US startups not chasing venture funding.


- Card issuance: Unlimited free physical and virtual cards
- Spend limits: Yes, by employee, vendor, or category; lockable to merchants
- Real-time visibility: Yes, with real-time policy flags
- Receipt capture: Yes, automated matching
- Accounting sync: QuickBooks, Xero, NetSuite, 200+ others
- Rewards: Up to 1.5% flat cashback, no annual fee
- Eligibility: Registered US entity (no sole proprietors), $25K+ in a connected US bank account; no personal guarantee
- Approval: Typically under 48 hours


### [2. Brex](https://www.brex.com/product/credit-card)


Built for venture-backed companies; now owned by Capital One (acquisition closed April 2026, so product details may shift).


- Card issuance: Unlimited employee cards, no extra cost
- Spend limits: Yes, custom policies by employee, department, category
- Real-time visibility: Yes
- Receipt capture: Yes, automated categorization
- Accounting sync: QuickBooks, Xero, NetSuite
- Rewards: Category points (up to 7x rideshare, 4x travel), not flat cashback
- Eligibility: Venture-backed with $50K+ cash reserves (monthly billing) or ~$1M+ revenue (daily payments); no personal guarantee


### [3. Airwallex](https://www.airwallex.com/global/spend-management/cards)


The most accessible option for bootstrapped or early-stage businesses.


- Card issuance: Unlimited physical and virtual Visa cards, free
- Spend limits: Yes, daily/monthly limits, merchant category blocking
- Real-time visibility: Yes, with real-time alerts
- Receipt capture: Yes, AI-driven matching
- Accounting sync: Xero, NetSuite, QuickBooks
- Rewards: Up to 2% cashback, 0% FX markup on held-currency spend
- Card type: Debit-style, spends from your held balance
- Eligibility: Any registered business; no minimum balance, no credit check


### [4. Chase Ink Business](https://creditcards.chase.com/business-credit-cards?iCELL=61GX)


The traditional US bank option.


- Card issuance: Employee cards free, but as authorized users on one shared account
- Spend limits: Limited individual controls, less granular than fintechs
- Real-time visibility: Standard online/mobile banking only
- Receipt capture: None built in
- Accounting sync: Statement export only
- Rewards: Flat 1.5% cashback, uncapped, plus 0% intro APR for 12 months
- Eligibility: Personal guarantee and credit check required


## The right corporate card saves more than money


Trace Cohen, co-founder and general partner at Six Point Ventures, has written that the corporate card decision quietly sets your expense policy, your finance team's workload, and how fast you close your books each month, which is a fair way to describe why this choice deserves more than a few minutes. The[full comparison is worth a read](https://valueaddvc.com/blog/ramp-vs-brex-vs-airbase-best-corporate-cards-and-spend-management-for-startups) if you're weighing credit limits against automation. If you're comparing UAE-specific platforms instead,[G2's Alaan vs. Pemo comparison](https://www.g2.com/compare/alaan-vs-pemo) is a useful side-by-side.


The pattern holds regardless of where you're based. A card that only handles payments leaves your finance team doing everything else by hand.[Forrester research cited by financial operations analysts found that companies using automated expense tools close their books up to 53% faster](https://www.houseblend.io/articles/ramp-brex-airbase-netsuite-integration) than those still reconciling manually. That gap is where most of the real cost sits, not in the annual fee or the rewards rate.


If you're running a small business in the UAE and you're tired of chasing receipts and reconciling spend by hand, the[Alaan Corporate Card](https://www.alaan.com/supercard) is built to take that off your plate. Set it up once, and let the controls do the rest.


## FAQs


**1. What are the eligibility criteria for a UAE corporate card?**
Conventional banks require a **valid trade license** , **6–12 months of trading history** , and a minimum annual revenue of AED 250,000 plus.


**2. Can new startups with zero trading history get a corporate card?**
Yes. While legacy banks require a 1-year history, digital platforms like **Alaan** and **Wio** issue virtual or physical cards immediately after account setup.


**3. What is the difference between a legacy bank card and a fintech card?**
Traditional cards offer revolving credit lines and reward points but require manual receipt tracking. Fintech cards like Alaan use pre-funded models with built-in receipt scanning and automated expense tracking.


**4. How do corporate cards help with UAE VAT and Corporate Tax?**
They create digital transaction logs and automate expense categorization. This provides the clean, traceable audit trail required for the **9% Corporate Tax** and simplifies input VAT recovery.


**5. Can I set individual spending limits for employee cards?**
Yes. Primary account holders can issue unlimited supplementary cards and configure strict monthly caps, single-transaction limits, or merchant restrictions per employee.
